name: lsu_accept
supersedes: protocol-v3.json (v1-v3 asked for a single acceptance structure over loads, copies and stores and found none; v4 asks one narrower question about stores only, with a probe that observes the issue stall directly instead of the last request's WAR release)
mechanisms: storage.global.store_queue (new engine rule, leaf fields on memory.store_l2.capacity): the LSU queue of pending global / local stores a warp's issue stalls on when it is full (ncu `stall_lg`)
question: Full-GPU attribution 2026-11-08 (full-gpu-chain-report.md §12): on cutlass_f16bf16_dense_tma_ws_06 the hardware spends 26 % of all warp-stall samples in `stall_lg` and 28.5 % of the samples sit on the epilogue's STG instructions; the engine lets a global store issue every cycle and only its own completion sees the store port, so the CTA retires ~1 k cycles early per wave (0.705; a diagnostic build gating store issue on a per-SMSP queue drained by the existing store path gives 0.943). lsu_accept v1 stg16 cells (both devices, six identical runs) show the WAR release of the D-th STG.128 flat up to D = 4 and jumping at D = 8 on h100 (26 -> 109 cycles, W = 1) and between D = 8 and 16 on b300, but the v1 window (one WAR on the last request) is non-monotone at D = 16 and cannot locate the knee. How many pending global-store requests does the LSU hold per SMSP (or per SM) before the next store's issue stalls, is the depth counted in requests or in sectors, and at what interval do pending stores leave the queue compared with the installed per-SM store port (memory.store_l2.service.sector_bytes_per_cycle, h100 31.65 / b300 32.19)?

engine_rules_declared_before_data.baseline: present engine (main 56712088 + task/fg-producer TMA queueing excess): a global / local store issues whenever its registers and scoreboards allow; MemoryHierarchy::store chains its sectors through the GPU-wide L2 write service and this SM's store port (store_l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle, outstanding_requests) and returns the acceptance cycle, which gates nothing of the warp.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.QS (per-SMSP store queue): every global / local store (MACC access_kind store, space global or local; atomics excluded -- storage.atomic.issue) occupies one entry of its SMSP's queue from its issue cycle until the store path has accepted its last sector (the `accept + occupancy` of MemoryHierarchy::store, i.e. after the shared L2 write service and this SM's store port); a store whose SMSP queue holds `store_l2.queue_requests` pending entries cannot issue (wait bucket resource, retry at the earliest pending acceptance). Leaf fields (memory.store_l2.capacity, schema memory_level): store_l2.queue_requests (count, measured), store_l2.queue_scope_smsp = 1.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.QM (per-SM store queue): as QS with one queue per SM shared by its four SMSPs; store_l2.queue_scope_smsp = 0, store_l2.queue_requests = the per-SM depth.
engine_rules_declared_before_data.sector variants: QS-sectors / QM-sectors: the queue counts 32 B sectors instead of requests (field store_l2.queue_sectors instead of queue_requests); chosen only if the stg4 knee sits at ~4x the stg16 knee (see derivation).
engine_rules_declared_before_data.prediction: stamped window (below), W warps on distinct SMSPs each issuing 24 STG back to back: the per-store issue gap g_k is flat (g0 ~ 2-4 cycles: STG issue + the clock read) for k <= Q and, once k > Q, equals the interval at which entries leave the queue. QS: the knee k* = Q + 1 does not move with W in {1, 2, 4} and halves at W = 8 (two warps per SMSP share the queue); QM: k* ~ Q_sm / W + 1. The drain gap beyond the knee is bytes_per_request / (store_l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle / W) if the SM port is the drain (per-SM drain shared by the W warps), i.e. grows linearly with W; stg4 (128 B requests) drains 4x faster than stg16 in cycles per request if the port is byte-bound.

probe: tools/microbench/lsu_accept/probe/store_queue.cu: one CTA of 32*W threads, W in {1, 2, 4, 8} (warp w on SMSP w % 4), bar.sync + fence.sc.gpu + bar.sync before every repetition (previous stores performed, queue empty), lane 0 of each warp records 25 %clock64 stamps: t_0 before the first store and t_k right after store k. Window = 24 back-to-back st.global on 24 distinct 64-bit pointer registers (per-lane coalesced, each request its own 128 B-aligned region, distinct per warp and per k; no sector shared), one clock read after every store, nothing else. Variants: stg16 (st.global.v4.b32, 512 B per request = 16 sectors), stg4 (st.global.b32, 128 B = 4 sectors). Samples per (variant, W, k): g_k = t_k - t_{k-1} over warps x launches x repetitions (first repetition of each launch dropped); row u = k, u = 0 carries the whole-window total. --launches 16 --reps 65, two runs per device.
sass_gate: tools/microbench/lsu_accept/sass_check_store_queue.py: in the repetition loop exactly 25 SR_CLOCKLO reads with exactly one STG of the variant's width between consecutive reads and no other memory / barrier / fence / branch instruction; the 24 STGs use 24 distinct address registers; control words recorded. A failing kernel disables its cells.
derivation: tools/microbench/lsu_accept/model_store_queue.py: per cell (variant, W) medians g_k; g0 = median(g_1, g_2, g_3); knee k* = the smallest k >= 2 with g_k >= max(2 g0, g0 + 6) and g_{k+1} >= max(2 g0, g0 + 6) (two consecutive slow gaps); no knee up to k = 24 -> cell 'deeper than 24' (unusable for Q). Q_cell = k* - 1; drain r_cell = median(g_k, k in k*+1 .. 24) cycles per request. Decisions, stg16 cells W in {1, 2, 4} (one warp per SMSP): (a) scope: Q_cell equal within +-1 across W -> QS with store_l2.queue_requests = median Q_cell; Q_cell(W) within +-1 of Q_cell(1) / W -> QM with queue_requests = Q_cell(1); neither -> none. W = 8 is recorded as a check against the chosen scope's prediction (QS: Q / 2 +- 1). (b) unit: stg4 Q_cell(W = 1) within +-1 of stg16 Q_cell(W = 1) -> requests; within +-25 % of 4x -> sectors (field queue_sectors = stg16 Q_cell x 16 sectors); neither -> record, install requests from stg16 only if (a) passed and the two runs agree. (c) repeatability: Q identical in the two runs of a device (exactly), r_cell within 15 % between runs. (d) drain: for the chosen scope, bandwidth_cell = W x 32 lanes x bytes_per_lane / r_cell; reported next to store_l2.sector_bytes_per_cycle x 32 B; agreement within 15 % at W in {1, 2, 4} means the installed port is the drain and the engine's existing store path stands; otherwise the deviation is recorded (the port leaf keeps its own protocol) and Q is still installed. First passing candidate in order is installed; none -> report, unrealised.
install: field registration in configs/schema_registry.json (memory_level: store_l2.queue_requests count, store_l2.queue_sectors count, store_l2.queue_scope_smsp flag), leaves in configs/mechanism_tree/<arch>/leaves/memory.store_l2.capacity.json (measured, source lsu_accept.<device>.v4r<n>), engine rule QS / QM as declared (per-unit deque of pending acceptance cycles; readiness check before register / scoreboard checks, wait bucket resource), CTest fixture (one warp, Q + 4 STG.128 behind a slow store port: the (Q+1)-th issues no earlier than the first's acceptance; two warps on distinct SMSPs do not share a QS queue), A/B full-gpu 500 x 2 and single-cluster 500 x 2 against the current baseline.
not_allowed: no case tuning; no change to the derivation after the data; a device whose runs fail the SASS gate or (c) stays disabled (enabled 0, queue not modelled) and is reported.

addenda.written: after h100-v4r1 / b300-v4r1 (sass gate 2 / 2 kernels pass on both; run-a == run-b on both)
addenda.text: (reading; decision none on both devices under the frozen request-count structures) stg16 W = 1 / 2: every gap 24 cycles, no knee up to 24 requests; W = 4: 32 for 8 requests then 64 (= 4 x 512 B / 31.65 B/cycle: the installed store port is the drain, drain_matches_installed_port = true on both devices); W = 8: 42-54 for 4 requests then 128. stg4: W = 1 / 2 / 4 gap 4 (W = 4 knees at 16 to 8 = 64 B/cycle aggregate); W = 8: 4 for 6 requests, 16 (64 B/cycle) to request ~17, then 32 (32 B/cycle). b300 identical in shape (stg16 W = 4 knee at 7, 28 -> 64; W = 8 at 4). The queue is neither a per-SMSP nor a per-SM request count: the knee moves with bytes issued (about 8-10 KB pending for 512 B requests, ~4 KB before a 64 B/cycle stage for 128 B requests) -- a per-SM byte queue in two stages (acceptance ~64 B/cycle with ~4 KB, drain = store port with ~5-6 KB). Established for the first time: a single SMSP issues STG.128 every 24 cycles and STG.32 every 4 (W = 1 and 2 alike), i.e. the store issue interval itself depends on the request's sectors. Both go to protocol v5 (two-stage byte queue + per-SMSP store issue interval by sectors).
